# Data by Figure

## Supplemental Figure 1

### SFig 1A: US Choropleth

Cumulative case counts per 100,000 people, Data as of March 05, 2024 at 2:00 pm EDT

Data from CDC Mpox Dashboard

```{r}
#load in the states data from the maps package, this gives you polygon coordinates for US states.
states_map <- map_data("state")

#check list of states
unique(states_map$region)

#load in case and case rate data 
us_state_case_data <- read_csv("r_map_data/us_case_rates_jan24.csv")

#join map with data 
us_map_data <- left_join(states_map, us_state_case_data, by = "region")

#plot the map
ggplot(us_map_data, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = case_rate)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "black") +
  coord_fixed(1.3) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "PuRd", direction = 1) +  
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Cumulative Cases in the Unites States by State", 
       fill= "Cases per 100,000 people") 
 


```

Case Rate Top 10\

```{r}
US_case_rate_table <- us_state_case_data %>%
  arrange(desc(case_rate)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  select(region, case_rate) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Top 10 U.S. States by Case Rate"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(
    columns = case_rate,
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    region = "State",
    case_rate = "Case Rate"
  ) %>%
  tab_options(
    table.font.names = "Helvetica",
    table.align = "center",
    heading.align = "center"
  )

# Save the table as a PDF
gtsave(US_case_rate_table, "US_case_rate_table.pdf")
```

### SFig 1B: US Cases and Vaccinations

Case data range 5/15/2022 through 4/20/2024

Vaccine data range 5/22/2022 through 01/06/2024

updated 10/15/25

```{r}
#read in csv file 
us_data <- read_csv("us_data_101525.csv")
# Assuming 'us_data' has columns: 'date_formated', 'count', 'type'
# 'type' has 1 = Cases, 2 = First Dose, 3 = Second Dose

#make sure the date column is the date class
us_data$date_formated <- as.Date(us_data$date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")
# Create a new dataset with a separate y-axis scale for First and Second Dose
us_data_line <- us_data[us_data$type %in% c(2, 3), ]

ggplot() +
  # Bar plot for Cases (type 1)
  geom_bar(data = us_data[us_data$type == 1, ], 
           aes(x = date_formated, y = count, fill = factor(type)), 
           stat = "identity", 
           position = "identity") +
  
  # Line plot for First Dose (type 2) and Second Dose (type 3)
  geom_line(data = us_data_line, 
            aes(x = date_formated, y = count/25, color = factor(type), group = type), 
            size = 0.8) +
  
  # Theme and titles
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "MPOX Cases and Vaccines Administered per Week in the US", 
       x = "Date", 
       y = "MPOX Cases", 
       fill = NULL, 
       color = "Vaccine Doses") +
  
  # Customize x-axis formatting
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b, %y", 
               date_breaks = "3 months"
               ) +
  
  # Manual color scale
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("1" = "seagreen3", "2" = "dodgerblue2", "3" = "red"),
                    labels = c("Cases", "First Dose", "Second Dose")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2" = "dodgerblue2", "3" = "red"), 
                     labels = c("First Dose", "Second Dose")) +
  
  # Adjust legend position and title
  theme(legend.position = c(0.85, 0.8),
        axis.title.x = element_text(family = "Arial", hjust = 0.5, size = 12, margin = margin(t = 15)),  # Change font family for x-axis
        axis.title.y = element_text(family = "Arial", hjust = 0.5, size = 12, margin = margin(r = 20)),  # Change font family for y-axis
        axis.text.x = element_text(family = "Arial", angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),  # Change font family for x-axis text
        axis.text.y = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 10),  # Change font family for y-axis text
        legend.title = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 10),  # Change font family for legend title
        legend.text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 9),    # Change font family for legend text
        plot.title = element_blank()) +  # Hide title
  # Create a second y-axis for First and Second Dose (lines), also includes the scale 
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ .*25, name = "Vaccine Doses",
                                         breaks = scales::pretty_breaks())) +
  theme(axis.title.y.right = element_text(margin = margin(l = 15)))
```

```{r}
#determine amount for each category in vizualization

#Type 1 Cases
us_data %>%
  filter(type == "1") %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count))

#Type 2 First vaccine Dose
us_data %>%
  filter(type == "2") %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count))

#Type 3 Second vaccine Dose
us_data %>%
  filter(type == "3") %>%
  summarise(total_count = sum(count))
```

### SFig 2C: Illinois Age Distribution

### SFig 2D: Illinois Race/Ethnicity

data request via Andrew English at IDPH

data range: May 2022 through April 2024

```{r}
#read in csv with two columns race_ethnicity and count
il_race_pie<-read.csv("illinois_race.csv")

#make sure the count is numeric

  "NHPI" = "#666666",
  "AIAN" = "#A6761D",
  "Multiple Races " = "#66A61E",
  "Unknown" = "#D95F02",
  "Asian" = "#7570B3",
```

```{r}
#import data
chicago_data <- read_csv("cdph_case_vax_data_101525.csv")

#correctly format dates
chicago_data$date_formated <- as.Date(chicago_data$Date, format = "%m/%d/%Y")

# Assuming 'chicago_data' has columns: 'date_formated', 'count', 'type'

) +

                    labels = c("Cases", "First Dose", "Second Dose")) +

theme(legend.position = c(0.85, 0.8),

        legend.text = element_text(family = "Arial", size = 9),    # Change font family for legend text
        plot.title = element_blank()) +  # Hide title
  # Create a second y-axis for First and Second Dose (lines), also includes the scale 
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = sec_axis(~ .*25, name = "Vaccine Doses",
                                         breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()))+
```

### Fig 1D: Chicago Test Positivity Howard Brown

data range June 2022- June 2024

from Howard brown, using data from MPOX_monthly_all, not stratified by MSM

```{r}
#read in csv with data for stacked bar
hb_mpox_tests <- read_csv("hb_mpox_tests.csv")

#ensure the 'year' and 'month' columns are numeric
hb_mpox_tests$year <- as.numeric(hb_mpox_tests$year)
hb_mpox_tests$month <- as.numeric(hb_mpox_tests$month)

#make a new column with month year
hb_mpox_tests$date <- as.Date(paste(hb_mpox_tests$year, hb_mpox_tests$month, "01", sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Change format to just "Year-Month"
hb_mpox_tests$year_month <- format(hb_mpox_tests$date, "%Y-%m")
```

```{r}

#read in data for rates line graph 
hb_mpox_rates <- read_csv("hb_mpox_rates.csv")

#make a new column with month year
hb_mpox_rates$date <- as.Date(paste(hb_mpox_rates$year, hb_mpox_rates$month, "01", sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Change format to just "Year-Month"
hb_mpox_rates$year_month <- format(hb_mpox_rates$date, "%Y-%m")


```

```{r}
#scaling for the y-axis
scale_factor <- 3.34

#plot both sets of data
ggplot()+
geom_bar(data = hb_mpox_tests, 
           aes(x = date, y = test_count, fill = factor(test_type)), 
           stat = "identity")  + 
  theme_classic() +
  labs(title = "MPOX test positivity", 
       x = "Date", 
       y = "Number of Tests", 
       fill = "Test Result") +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(min(hb_mpox_tests$date), max(hb_mpox_tests$date), by = "1 month"),
    labels = function(d) {
      first_date <- min(hb_mpox_tests$date)
      months_since_start <- as.integer((year(d) - year(first_date)) * 12 + month(d) - month(first_date))
      lbls <- ifelse(months_since_start %% 3 == 0, format(d, "%Y-%b"), "")
      return(lbls)
    }
  ) +
   geom_line(data = hb_mpox_rates, 
            aes(x = date, y = pos_rate*scale_factor), 
            color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = hb_mpox_rates, 
             aes(x=date, y=pos_rate*scale_factor), size = 1.5, shape = 21, fill = "black") +
  labs(title = NULL, x = "Date", y = "Test Positivity %", color = "Test Positivity") +
  
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("1" = "orange", "2" = "grey"),  
    labels = c("Positive", "Negative")) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.85, 0.8)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
  name = "Number of Tests",                     # Primary y-axis label
  breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 50),              # Customize increments (adjust range as needed)
  sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor,       # Transformation back for secondary axis
                      name = "Test Positivity %",
                      breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20))  # Secondary axis increments
)

```

## Figure 2

### Fig 2A: CDPH STI Data

Male only cases of STI per month from CDPH, data from Jeff Lauritsen 7/23/2024 [Jeff.Lauritsen\@cityofchicago.org](mailto:Jeff.Lauritsen@cityofchicago.org)

Data used was Male only

```{r}
#data is stratified by test type according to the following key: 1- Chlamydia, 2- Gonorrhea, 3- Syphilis, 4- HIV, 5- Mpox

#read in data file 
cdph_sti_data <- read.csv("cdph_sti_data.csv")

#formatting the data
#ensure the 'year' and 'month' columns are numeric
cdph_sti_data$Year <- as.numeric(cdph_sti_data$Year)
cdph_sti_data$Month <- as.numeric(cdph_sti_data$Month)

#make a new column with month year
cdph_sti_data$date <- as.Date(paste(cdph_sti_data$Year, cdph_sti_data$Month, "01", sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Change format to just "Year-Month"
cdph_sti_data$year_month <- format(cdph_sti_data$date, "%Y-%m")
cdph_sti_data$year_month <- as.Date(paste0(cdph_sti_data$year_month, "-01"))

#make sure test_type is a factor
cdph_sti_data$test_type <- factor(cdph_sti_data$test_type,
                                levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
                                labels = c("Chlamydia", "Gonorrhea", "Syphilis", "HIV", "Mpox"))

```

```{r}
#plot data
ggplot(data = cdph_sti_data, aes(x = year_month, y = pos_cases, color = test_type, group = test_type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Positive Cases Per Month in 2022 by Test Type",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Positive Cases",
    color = "Test Type"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 months",
    date_labels = "%b"  # Optional: Formats as "Jan 2023", etc.
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Chlamydia" = "seagreen3",
      "Gonorrhea" = "dodgerblue2",
      "Syphilis" = "maroon2",
      "HIV" = "goldenrod1",
      "Mpox" = "darkorchid1"
    )
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotates labels for readability
```

```{r}
hb_sti_data$month <- as.numeric(hb_sti_data$month)

#make a new column with month year
hb_sti_data$date <- as.Date(paste(hb_sti_data$year, hb_sti_data$month, "01", sep = "-"), format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Change format to just "Year-Month"
hb_sti_data$year_month <- format(hb_sti_data$date, "%Y-%m")
hb_sti_data$year_month <- as.Date(paste0(hb_sti_data$year_month, "-01"))

#make sure test_type is a factor
hb_sti_data$test_type <- factor(hb_sti_data$test_type,
                                levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
                                labels = c("Chlamydia", "Gonorrhea", "Syphilis", "HIV", "Mpox"))


```

```{r}
    x = "Date",
    y = "Positive Rate",
```

```{r}
#read in data

#filter to 2022 data only 
radar_data_2022 <- radar_data %>% filter(year == 2022)

```

Total sex partners in the last 6 months

"vasexpartners_p6m" = Number of vaginal/anal sex partners in the past 6 months

includes longitudinal data

```{r}
#filter out data to only include the first response by the participant in 2022
radar_data_2022_first <- radar_data_2022 %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  slice_min(order_by = month, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#check data distribution via a histogram
hist(radar_data_2022_first$vasexpartners_p6m,
     main = "Histogram of Number of Sex Partners",
     xlab = "Number of Sex Partners",
     col = "lightblue",
     breaks = 20)


#view the stats
radar_data_2022_first %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    min = min(vasexpartners_male_p6m, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(vasexpartners_male_p6m, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(vasexpartners_male_p6m, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(vasexpartners_male_p6m, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    max = max(vasexpartners_male_p6m, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

#View stats using Tukey’s 5-number summary
#Returns: minimum, lower-hinge (Q1), median, upper-hinge (Q3), and maximum.
fivenum(radar_data_2022_first$vasexpartners_male_p6m)

#stats
#test for significant difference between months using Kruskal-Wallis Test (non-parametric ANOVA) use this because the data is heavily right skewed 
kruskal.test(vasexpartners_p6m ~ as.factor(month), data = radar_data_2022_first)


```

Pseudo log scale (due to zero values)

```{r}

ggplot(radar_data_2022_first, aes(x = as.factor(month), y = vasexpartners_p6m)) +

  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, color = "blue") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(base = 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sex Partners in the Last 6 Months",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Number of Sex Partners (pseudo-log scale)"
  ) +
```

```{r}
  # Bar plot for Cases (type 1)
```

## Table 1

### NMH Cohort Demographics

```{r}
#Read the CSV file into a data frame
dem_table <- read.csv("021125_demtable.csv")
col_var <- colnames(dem_table)
print(col_var)

# Convert colnames to lower case
names(dem_table) <- tolower(names(dem_table))   


dem_table <- replace(dem_table, dem_table == "Patient declined to respond", "Unknown")
dem_table <- replace(dem_table, dem_table == "Patient unable to respond", "Unknown")


dem_table <- dem_table %>%
  mutate(
    msm = recode(msm, "1" = "Yes", "2" = "No", "3" = "Unknown")  # change labels
  )

dem_table <- dem_table %>%
  mutate(
    sex = fct_infreq(sex),  # Reorder 'sex' by frequency
    msm = fct_infreq(msm),  # Reorder 'msm' by frequency
    dem_race = fct_infreq(dem_race),  # Reorder 'dem_race' by frequency
    dem_ethnicity = fct_infreq(dem_ethnicity),  # Reorder 'dem_ethnicity' by frequency
    pt_encounter = fct_infreq(pt_encounter)  # Reorder 'pt_encounter' by frequency
  )
# Create a tbl_summary using your data
table1 <- dem_table %>%
  tbl_summary(
    include = c(age, sex, msm, dem_race, dem_ethnicity, pt_encounter),
    missing = "no",
    type = list(
      age ~ "continuous", 
      sex ~ "categorical", 
      msm ~ "categorical", 
      dem_race ~ "categorical", 
      dem_ethnicity ~ "categorical", 
      pt_encounter ~ "categorical"
    ), 
    label = list(
      age = "Age",              # Relabel 'age'
      sex = "Sex Assigned at Birth",                   # Relabel 'sex'
      msm = "Men who have Sex with Men", # Relabel 'msm'
      dem_race = "Race",      # Relabel 'dem_race'
      dem_ethnicity = "Ethnicity",      # Relabel 'dem_ethnicity'
      pt_encounter = "Patient Point of Care" # Relabel 'pt_encounter'
    )
  ) %>%
  modify_header(
    all_stat_cols() ~ "**Patients**", 
    label= "**Variable**", # Fix: Modify all statistics columns header
    all_stat_cols() ~ paste0("**Patients**\n(N = ", nrow(dem_table), ")")  # Modify column label with N
  ) %>%
  bold_labels()
  
# Print the summary table
table1

# Convert table1 to gt table format
gt_table1 <- as_gt(table1)

# Save the gt table as a PNG -this has to be run in the console
gt::gtsave(gt_table1, "Table1.png")

```

## Table 2

### NMH Cohort Vaccine, Treatment and STI Data

```{r}
#Read the CSV file into a data frame
vax_table <- read.csv("table2.csv")
col_var2 <- colnames(vax_table)
print(col_var2)

#make table
table2 <- vax_table %>%
  tbl_summary(
    include = c(vax_doses, vax_1_before, vax_1_before_days, vax_1_after, vax_1_after_days, med_tpoxx, concur_active_4, comorb_hivstatus, sti_hiv_prep, sti_hiv_art),
    by = mpox_year,
    missing = "no",
    type = list(
      vax_doses ~ "categorical",
      vax_1_before ~ "categorical",
      vax_1_before_days ~ "continuous",
      vax_1_after ~ "categorical",
      vax_1_after_days ~ "continuous",
      med_tpoxx ~ "categorical",
      concur_active_4 ~ "categorical",
      comorb_hivstatus ~ "categorical",
      sti_hiv_prep ~ "categorical",
      sti_hiv_art ~ "categorical"
    ),
    label = list(
      vax_doses = "Total vaccine doses received",
      vax_1_before = "First dose of vaccine administered prior to infection",
      vax_1_before_days = "Days vaccine administered prior to infection",
      vax_1_after = "First dose of vaccine administered post infection",
      vax_1_after_days = "Days vaccine administered post infection",
      med_tpoxx = "Received tecovirimat",
      concur_active_4 = "Positive test indicated for active STI infection",
      comorb_hivstatus = "Patient has a confirmed HIV diagnosis",
      sti_hiv_prep = "Patient is currently on PREP",
      sti_hiv_art = "Patient is currently on ART"
    )
  ) %>%
  modify_table_body(
    ~ .x %>%
      filter(
        !(
          (variable == "med_tpoxx" | variable == "vax_1_before" | variable == "vax_1_after" | variable == "concur_active_4" | variable == "comorb_hivstatus" | variable == "sti_hiv_prep" | variable == "sti_hiv_art") &
          row_type == "level" & 
          label != "yes"
        )
      )
  ) %>%
  modify_header(label = "**Variable**") %>%
  bold_labels()


#look at the table 
table2


# Convert table1 to gt table format
gt_table2 <- as_gt(table2)

# Save the gt table as a PNG -this has to be run in the console
gt::gtsave(gt_table2, "Table2.png")

```

## Figure 3

### Fig 3A: NMH Cohort Map

Patient cohort case counts per 100,000 people from 5/15/2022 to 4/30/2024

Note that 18/108 patients did not reside in Chicago and 6/18 were out of state

```{r}
#load in Healthy Chicago Equity Zones csv with geometry
hez_df <- read_csv("r_map_data/Healthy_Chicago_Equity_Zones_20250515.csv")

#the sf package allows standard for encoding geographic vector data.
hez_sf <- st_as_sf(hez_df, wkt = "Geometry", crs = 4326)

#import cases and rates for nmh patients in hez zones

nmh_hez_rates <- read_csv("r_map_data/nmh_chicago_case_rate.csv")

#join map with data 
chicago_map_data <- left_join(hez_sf, nmh_hez_rates, by = "Equity Zone")
 
#plot map 
ggplot(chicago_map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), color = "black") +  
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "PuRd", direction = 1) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "NMH Cases in Chicago per Health Equity Zone", fill = "Cases per 100,000")
```

### 2 page format

```{r}

# Import data
ncbi_accession_mpxv <- read_csv("ncbi_accession_mpxv.csv")

# Split data into two equal sections
n <- ceiling(nrow(ncbi_accession_mpxv) / 2)

ncbi_accession_mpxv_1 <- ncbi_accession_mpxv %>%
  slice(1:n)

ncbi_accession_mpxv_2 <- ncbi_accession_mpxv %>%
  slice((n + 1):n())

# Function to format both tables
format_ncbi_table <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_header(
      title = "Mpox Virus Isolate Accession Numbers"
    ) %>%
    cols_label(
      isolate_id = "Isolate ID",
      ncbi_submission_id = "NCBI Submission ID",
      ncbI_accession_number = "GenBank Accession Number",
      bioproject = "BioProject ID",
      sra_accession = "BioSample Accession"
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(color = "#000000"),
      locations = cells_body()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(
        color = "#000000",
        weight = "bold"
      ),
      locations = list(
        cells_column_labels(),
        cells_title(groups = "title")
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(11),
      data_row.padding = px(3),
      column_labels.padding = px(5),
      table.border.top.color = "#000000",
      table.border.bottom.color = "#000000",
      heading.border.bottom.color = "#000000",
      column_labels.border.top.color = "#000000",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = "#000000",
      table_body.border.top.color = "#000000",
      table_body.border.bottom.color = "#000000"
    )
}

# Create both tables
gt_ncbi_accessions_1 <- format_ncbi_table(ncbi_accession_mpxv_1)
gt_ncbi_accessions_2 <- format_ncbi_table(ncbi_accession_mpxv_2)

# Display tables
gt_ncbi_accessions_1
gt_ncbi_accessions_2

# Export tables as separate PNG files
gtsave(
  gt_ncbi_accessions_1,
  "STable_1_Page1.png"
)

gtsave(
  gt_ncbi_accessions_2,
  "STable_1_Page2.png"
)

# View original dataset
View(ncbi_accession_mpxv)

```
